newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Telebras rises 1.0 pct in morning trade.
newsitem.headline: Telebras rises 1.0 pct in morning trade.

text.p: Preferred shares of bellwether Telebras were 1.0 percent higher in light morning trade on the Sao Paulo bourse following the release of the firm's nine-month earnings, brokers said.
Telebras traded at 81.20 reais, while its common shares rose 1.67 percent to 68.01 reais, leading the Bovespa index to rise 0.5 percent to 67,308 points at 1300 local/1500 GMT.
Market turnover was 154.9 million reais ($150.7 million).
Earlier today Telebras announced a 1.980 billion real net consolidated profit in the first nine months of the year.

Telebras' earnings were in line with most market estimates, though some analysts noted Telebras could have performed better if Telerj, the firm's unit serving Rio de Janeiro state, had not made provisions to cover expenses with its voluntary retirement plan, which affected Telerj's and Telebras' profits.

Analysts continue optimistic about the company's earnings prospects for 1996, with estimates for Telebras' consolidated profits ranging between 2.6 billion reais and 2.8 billion reais, still reflecting last year's telephone rate hike and an increase in call volumes.

Shares of Telebras' subsidiaries fell earlier after yesterday's strong rally, except for Telerj preferred which continued its uptrend, rising 2.72 percent to 113 reais. reais, while Telemig stock fell 2.15 percent to 136 reais.
Analysts said stocks of Telebras' units had risen sharply on Tuesday following the publication of cellular concession rules favourable to the company's subsidiaries.
